widgets_values:
# Floor plan -> 3D -> render passes

**Any plan image in; a clean, metric GLB and every pass the renders
need out.** Nothing here spends credits; both recognisers are local
models.

**How it reads the plan.** Image-to-3D models (TRELLIS, Hunyuan3D,
Tripo) rebuild single objects as blobby, unscaled meshes; they cannot
read a plan. So this goes plan -> vector walls -> exact extrusion:

1. a CubiCasa5K segmenter marks **wall / door / window** pixels and
   ignores furniture, text and dimension lines (`recogniser = cv` is a
   model-free fallback for clean CAD exports);
   **Raster2Seq** (SIGGRAPH '26, `room_model`) reads the **rooms**:
   they become the zones, and where two rooms meet with a solid
   straight line drawn between them but no wall found, that line
   becomes a partition (WC / storage hairlines). Dotted curtain
   tracks, text and furniture are skipped. `room_walls` off = rooms
   as zones only; `room_model = none` = walls only, as before;
2. walls are vectorised and **snapped to the plan axes**, so they come
   out as crisp prisms (~2k triangles for the whole showroom);
3. door gaps get a lintel, window gaps a sill and a lintel, each zone
   a floor slab; exterior walls are split by side (`ext_north` ..
   `ext_west`, lintels too), so `ext_south*` in HIDE PARTS is a cutaway;
4. an **ID twin** paints every part in its zone colour (red, green,
   blue, yellow, magenta, cyan) for the regional-prompt masks.

**Your steps.**
1. Load your plan in 1.1 (north up). Set `plan_width_m` to the real
   west-east outer width (the overall dimension) and `wall_height`.
2. Run. Check **1.3 understood**: walls black, door gaps orange,
   window gaps blue, zones tinted.
3. Missed a partition? Right-click the plan in 1.1 -> *Open in
   MaskEditor*, paint over it, save, Run: the mask is wired to
   `add_walls`. Something read as a wall that is not (racks, a
   heavy bench)? Paint it on a copy loaded in 1.2 and wire that mask
   to `erase`.
4. Zones are the rooms Raster2Seq read (largest first: red, green,
   blue, yellow, magenta, cyan; the rest white), named in the report.
   For your own functional zones, paint a plan-sized image with flat
   red / green / ... regions, load it in 1.2, wire IMAGE -> `zone_map`:
   it overrides the rooms. An added partition you do not want: paint
   it into `erase`, or switch `room_walls` off.

GLBs land in `output/plan3d/` (`plan_3d.glb`, `plan_3d_ids.glb`);
passes in `output/plan3d/passes/`. Built with
`python tools/build_workflow_plan3d.py`.

widgets_values:
## 2  Free camera

Same chain as the showroom's 5.13. **HIDE PARTS** lists the parts to
leave out (one per line, `*` `?` wildcards, `#` comment); it drives
both GLB Part Filters, so depth and zone masks always agree. The
report (1.4) and `part names in the model` list what you can name:
`ext_north` .. `ext_west` (+ `_door_lintels`, `_window_lintels`,
`_window_sills`), `walls_interior`, `door_lintels`, `floor_z<n>`,
`ceiling`.

Orbit / pan / zoom the **Preview 3D (Advanced)** viewer, press Run:
its camera bakes depth, normal and ID at 1664 x 928. Prefer numbers?
Wire `camera by numbers` (target = the centre in the report) to
camera_info on all three Render Mesh nodes.

The six zone masks come from the ID pass by channel thresholds
(red = R - G - B, yellow = R x G - B, ...), exactly as in the zoned
showroom workflow: drop them into ConditioningSetMask.

widgets_values:
## 3  Fixed cameras

Six cameras the plan node frames from the model's size: four
isometrics at 35 degrees, a near-vertical top view and an eye-level
view from the west end looking east. They see the same HIDE PARTS
list as the free camera. Each saves depth, normal and ID to
`output/plan3d/passes/<camera>_<pass>`.
